The engineer informs me that it will be completed in the month oE September.
Ontario-Collingwood, improvements in harbour, $50,000.
Has Mr. Coste, the government engineer, valued the Collingwood dry dock, and if so, what is the valuation ?
That is not connected with this item, but I will be glad to get the information later.
Surely the minister would remember.
I do not.
Is it correct, as reported, that Mr. Coste has valuea the dry dock at $540,000 ?
I cannot remember, but I will bring the information down to-morrow.
It is a matter of very great importance if we have to pay for thirty or forty years 4 per cent on $540,uoo.
I will bring the information down to-morrow.
What is this item for ?
To complete the widening of the channel which is under contract at present.
When will it be finished and how much is required to finish it ?

This amount is to complete the work

carried.
It won't pass in that cavalier way.
What does the hon. gentleman mean by ' cavalier ' ? I am delighted to give the hon. gentleman all the information I can.
The minister should not call ' carried ' without replying to the question asked. Collingwood is a very important harbour and it is the duty of the minister to give the information we require.
The total amount of the contract is $87,000, there was paid upon that $49,000, and this is to complete the balance of the work.
What is the depth and width of the channel ?
Twenty-one feet deep and 220 feet wide for the whole distance of the harbour and for some distance outside.
If a boat gets out of the channel what will be the depth of the water at the side ?
It would vary from twelve to fifteen feet.
The first channel was 110 feet wide, and now it is being enlarged to 220 feet. How much remains to be completed ?
Judging by the expenditure, about one-half.

This has nothing to do with the bonus for the dry dock.
Mr; HYMAN. Nothing at all.
Who has the contract ?
Boone.

There were a good many complaints last year, but I do not think the contractor was entirely to blame because he had a great many difficulties to overcome. Taking everything into account I think he did very well. Some were very strongly of the opinion that the Minister of Public Works should take the work from him, but I do not think so at all. I think he was making a reasonable effort to get along with the work as best he could.
Mr. [DOT] HYMAN. I think these complaints were made two years ago. Last year and this year so far as the department is concerned, the work has been proceeded with in a satisfactory manner.
Is it dredging, or rock work now ?
The engineer informs me that the present work is principally rock work.
Has Mr. Broone any dredges other than he had last year, or is he working .with the same plant ?
The same plant, so far as the department is aware.
Is he progressing at the usual rate according to your progress estimates ?
The engineer informs me that the work is progressing satisfactorily.

Collingwood is a very important port and every reasonable effort should be made to get the work done promptly. The people will be glad to know that the work is likely to be finished at an early date, and that the harbour will be in a proper shape to enable them to carry on their business successfully.
Depot Harbour breakwater, $100,000.
What is the total cost of this work ?
The total contract is $157,500 and there is some rip-rap work for foundation amounting to $37,500. The contract was let on the 14th of May, 1902, to Messrs. Davis, Haney & Miller.
What are the dimensions of this breakwater ?
The addition is 120 feet long, 80 feet wide and from 29 to 50 feet high. It runs from the main land towards the island.
Practically it is a present to the Canada Atlantic Railway.
When was that amount first voted ? I see that the same amount was in the estimates last year, and no money was expended.
The contract was let last year.
What is the amount of the contract ?
Did the government purchase the land ?
I am informed that the wharf is being built at the foot of a public road, so that there is no necessity for purchasing the land.
It belongs to somebody, of course ?
It is open to everybody.
I do not think that follows. On a public road you must get liberty the same as anywhere else.
I do not suppose that it is possible to close the road, and therefore it will always be open to the public.
If the minister has obtained an opinion from the Department of Justice to that effect, we must bow to it, but I have very great doubt about it.
Is this to complete the work ?
No, there will be a small amount left.
I do not understand why the department does not take the whole amount now.
We are taking the difference in the supplementary estimates.
When does the contract for Depot Harbour call for completion ?
Early this fall.
The parties who did the work last year were Haney, Davis and Miller. Is that the same Davis who did the Cornwall canal business ?

I understand not. This is J. P. Davis.
Ontario-Gananoque, dredging, $5,000.
Will the minister explain this ?
It is for the purpose of increasing the depth of the harbour from 10 to 15 feet. The work was commenced this year and this is to complete it.
Is this being done by contract or by days' work ?

It is being done by a rented dredge at the rate of 13J cents a yard.
Ontario-Goderich harbour works, $20,000.
What is the total amount of the contract ?
$20,000. This vote is for repairs to the north pier.
Is it all for repairs ? Mr. HYMAN. All but about $2,000 for dredging.
Is it intended to ask for tender for this work, less what there may be for dredging ?

The work is made up or some six or seven different items. It is almost impossible to have a work of this kind done by contract. It is being done under the engineers of the department by days' work. There is a special engineer in charge of the work.
What amount was expended last year and what was the result ?
The work last year was on the south pier.
The amount Toted last year was not for repairs, but for the construction of a breakwater.
I understand that the vote of last year was for repairs.

The hon. gentleman is misinformed or wrong information was given last year. It was to the effect that the vote was to construct 200 feet of a breakwater as a trial. The minister in charge of the estimates said that if that was found to be a valuable work, it would possibly be continued. How was the money expended, and what was the result ?
$12,000 of this is a revote. $S,000 was spent on the repairs. Only $8,000 is being asked for this year.
Is there anything in the supplementary estimates for 1905 ?
There is nothing in this work for the supplementary estimates.
For another work there ?
For the extension of the breakwater there but nothing for this.
Was there any money expended last year on the breakwater 1
Not on the new breakwater.
How was that ? The money was voted for that purpose.
It is being revoted now and the contract has been let for the work which is now being proceeded with. The timber is being got out for the work but no money has been expended.
What is the length of the pier ?
500 feet.

It would seem to me that when a certain amount of money is to be expended on an important harbour like Goderich there should be some general information given to the committee as to how much money will be required to complete the harbour and make it worthy of the people of Canada. This system of putting in $20,000 this year and $20,000 next year, &c., makes it rather unsatisfactory to the committee and cannot be in the interests of the people of that neighbourhood. Last year the hon. gentleman having charge of the estimates said that it was proposed to spend $20,000 on the new breakwater. The .minister of Public Works at page 13240 of last year's ' Hansard ' said :
This matter has been taken up not alone by the Goderich people but by the large business Mr. HYMAN.	,
and commercial interests of Ontario, especially from Toronto west who represent in the strongest manner the importance of this work. I am asking for this vote of $20,000 for the purpose of making a trial of 200 feet of breakwater.
There is the statement of the hon. minister, It may be that the hon. gentleman will keep this going for many years. It has been going now for many years.

The explanation of the item is simply this, that the breakwater to which the hon. gentleman alludes has been contracted for but on the old breakwater certain repairs were needed and $8,000 were expended on this last year. There are two separate works and the intention of the department is to proceed immediately with the construction of the new breakwater which is now under contract.
Did I understand the minister to say that $8,000 of the $20,000 voted last year for the construction of 200 feet of a breakwater was expended on repairs ?
There was a larger item $20,000 last year, an item of $30,000, which was in different appropriations and of this $8,000 was expended on repairs to the south breakwater.
Then the $20,000 voted last year was not expended at all ?
No.
Out of what vote was the $8,000 expended ?
I am informed that the amount expended for repairs was in the supplementary, not in the main estimates.
When will the Goderich harbour be completed ?

That is a somewhat difficult question to answer. The reports of the engineers in regard to Goderich are that before a complete work is made, at least a thousand feet of the new breakwater will be required. The contract which has been entered into by the department at the present time is for 500 feet of that breakwater. If that is not found sufficient it will then be a matter for the department to decide whether they will extend the breakwater to a thousand feet or not.

I do not want to continue the discussion beyond saying that last year the statement of the minister was that it was proposed to make an experiment here with 200 feet of breakwater at a cost of $20,000. I understand the minister to say the $20,000 was not expended. They are proposing now by the statement of the hon. gentleman to try 500 feet. They are going to make an expenditure very much larger before they ascertain whether the breakwater will be suitable or not. If it was necessary in the interests of the country to

experiment with 200 feet I do not think it is in the interests of the people that the department should now experiment with 500 feet.

The only explanation I have in regard to the matter is that the engineers of the department reported, after looking into the matter carefully in different states of the weather, that it might require 1,000 feet of breakwater but that 500 feet would be quite necessary in the interests of the department and the public, and a contract was entered into for 500 feet, in the hope that it will be sufficient and that the balance will not be necessary.
What became of the balance of the vote of last year ?

We are revoting $12,000. Hon. gentlemen will understand that these estimates were made up some time since. This vote should have been for a larger amount than $12,000, but it was expected that more of the vote available in the department would have been expended before the end of the fiscal year and consequently there appears a vote of only $12,000.
Could the minister give any idea of the total amount of this expenditure ?
There is a contract for 500 feet. If my memory serves me the contract amounts to $71,000 or $72,000.
What amount of shipping goes into that port ?

I have not the details but I may say that Goderich is one of the most important ports on Lake Huron. There is a large elevator there now which is being served by the Grand Trunk Railway at the present time and the Canadian Pacific Railway are extending their line so as to reach Goderich harbour ; I presume the amount of shipping will increase when they get there. I understand it is the intention of the Canadian Pacific Railway to make Goderich a large receiving and shipping port.
When and to whom was this contract let ?
Battle & Conlon, the lowest tenderers. The amount of the tender is $74,000.
How many tenders were received ?
I have not the information here, but I shall be glad to give it later on.
Information given after the money is voted is interesting, but it is more interesting when given before ,thei money is voted.

It was given to the lowest tenderer.
Mr. iSPROULE. Is the $16,000 spent last year included in this contract, or was that for something else ?
It was not included. This is a straight contract for the building of 500 feet of breakwater at Goderich. There has been no expenditure under that contract:
What became of the $16,000 over and above the repairs ?

I am sorry that I have been unable to explain the matter to the satisfaction of the hon. gentleman (Mr. Sproule). It is stated in the estimates that this is a revote of $12,000. The hon. gentleman will understand that these estimates were made up very early in the year. It was then expected that there would be a larger sum expended upon the amount available to the department, that the contract would be let on certain money earned. But the preparing of the plans and calling for tenders took longer than was expected, and the work did not go on. Otherwise the amount would have been larger than $12,000. This is a revote of $12,000.

That is practically no explanation at all. Last year $36,000 was voted for this work at Goderich. Out of this the minister tells us he spent $8,000 in repairs. That left him $28,000. Now, if $12,000 of that is revoted, that leaves $16,000 that must have been spent for some purpose, because it does not appear in the revote and is not in the estimates. What was it spent for ?

It may have been revoted. It is not spent. If this item were made up to-day, or if the department had known the exact expenditure that would have been made up to the end of the fiscal year, it would have read ' Goderich harbour works, revote, $28,000.' But $16,000 of the money lapsed.
That is what you revote.
We revote $12,000 and $16,000 lapsed.

But why do you revote
$12,000 ?

Because it was thought that the expenditure for the year ending 30th June, 1904, would be larger than it actually proved to be.
air. LENNOX. If we had known all we know now we would have had a revote of $28,000 instead of a revote of $12,000 V

That is practically correct-only $8,000 was expended.
air. LENNOX. We voted $36,000 last year and spent $8,000. That would leave $28,000. Should we not amend this item, and make it plain that it is a revote of $20,000 instead of a revote of $12,000 ? In its present form it is misleading. If you change that to a revote of $28,000 you will have to

776<X
change the other column to make it correspond. The result is.that we are voting less this year than last year.
Sixteen thousand dollars has lapsed.
Is it all lapsed ?
We revote $12,000.
It is all lapsed except the $8,000 that has been expended. That is correct, is it not ?

The total vote last year was $36,000, of which $8,000 was spent. We might have revoted $28,000, but we only revoted $12,000 owing to the fact that when the estimates were made up we thought the expenditure would be larger. But we make a revote of $12,000 and an additional vote of $8,000.

If we are revoting at all, we should revote to the whole extent of the vote of this year, so long as it is within the limits of the lapsed vote. You could revote to the extent of $28,000. As a matter of fact, you are revoting $20,000.
We are only revoting $12,000. Surely the hon. gentleman will see that of the amount of $20,000, $12,000 is a revote and $8,000 is new.

The mere fact that the hon. minister puts it down as $12,000 does not make it so. There was a lapsed vote of $28,000. Anything that you vote to-night up to $28,000 is a revote, however it may be put in the estimates. But you should make the estimates accord with the facts.

That is right-otherwise this is misleading the House. We voted last year so much. At the end of the fiscal year everything voted and not spent lapsed. So, to the extent of the unspent amount, any money voted this year is a revote. If this is done in every case, we know what we are giving in addition to what was given last year. We know7 what we are doing.
This ought to be amend ed
Carried.

I want the chairman to understand that if he wishes straight sailing he will have to treat us properly. When a gentleman is speaking it is not proper for the chairman to throw ' carried ' in his face. I protest against that. Now, I want to say to the minister, through the chairman, that it is not consistent or proper that we should deal with an item in the way it is here proposed. We have the minister's bald statement that we are revoting $12,000 and making a new vote of $8,000 besides, a total of $20,000. Now, the fact is we are revoting $20,000 of a lapsed vote of $28,000. I submit to the committee that that item should be changed before we go any further Mr. LENNOX.
if the committee has any regard for consistency or any desire to put the facts on record as they actually exist.

We have an extra column put in the estimates to enable us to keep track of what money we vote from year to year, how much has been expended and how much is intended to be expended in the future. Now, if this column that is headed ' revote ' means anything or is worth anything, we ought to have put dowrn here the amount actually revoted. Contrary to the custom, in a great many cases this year, it is improperly put down, and so the House is misled. It takes much more trouble to-get at the information, and even then we do not get it as clearly as if it were put down in the estimates as it ought to be.
I move that this item be amended by changing so as to show that this is a revote of $20,000.
This resolution reads ' Goderich harbour, $20,000.' Of that one-fifth has been already voted. We are now asked to vote $10,000, and it is for the committee to say whether that is to be voted oi' not.

Is it the intention to spend only $20,000 this year ? I understand the position the minister takes, that so much money was expected to be expended by the 1st of July, and that was expended when these estimates were made up. Now I ask whether the government intends to spend the lapsed amount in addition to the $8,000.
' Mr. HYMAN. Whatever is in the supplementary estimates. That is the total amount that we are permitted to expend.

Now that the Finance Minister has come in, I want to appeal to him with regard to these items. For the purpose of enabling the House t,o understand how the money is voted and used, we have the estimates made up with three columns of figures. One gives the full amount of money voted for the work last year ; the last column gives the amount supposed to be voted this year, and the third column to the left shows how much of the money voted last year is to be revoted this year because it was not spent. In this case according to our calculation, there ought to be a revote of $28,000 because there has been only $8,000 of it spent in repairs ; but it shows in this case a revote of $12i,0i00>. Now, either there is a purpose in having this additional column or else it is useless. The purpose has been to enable us to understand how much of the money lapsed at the end of the financial year and how much was spent during the year we require to revote for that work. Now this is misleading, because any one would come to the conclusion that out of this $36,000 all was spent but $12,000, whereas the minister says only $8,000 was srent. We want to know whe-

ther it is the intention to have the estimates made and kept in a proper way, or jumbled up in such a way that we do not know what we are voting.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I have not heard the explanation of the Minister of Public Works, but I know there is no jumbling up and no hap-hazard way about it. These main estimates were made up months ago. The only judgment to be formed was as to the amount which was likely to be spent during the financial year. My hon. friend says a revote should be made of the money1 which has lapsed at the close of the financial year. That would be correct if the estimates were prepared at the close of the financial year, when you know exactly how much money you have spent. But when you make up your estimates early in the year, say in the month of January, and the main estimates were begun earlier than that, you can only form a reasonable judgment as to what amount is likely to be spent, and when we reach the end of the financial year it may turn out that the actual expenditure has been different from that anticipated. The statement for the revote therefore made some months ago was made in perfect good faith, but the events of the six months since intervening might largely change the figure, and the actual expenditure might prove to be different from what was expected. There is no lack of good faith I can assure my hon. friend.

But when the estimates were made up it was in the winter time. You could not do this class of work in the winter time, therefore it was within the knowledge of the minister or the heads of the departments that it was utterly impossible to spend the money for this work for which he is asking money now. Therefore it must be revoted if they intend to use it\ for the coming year. We would naturally expect that the amount of money not spent would appear as a revote ; otherwise what is the purpose of having a column of revotes ? It does not give the House any intelligent information if it is made up in that way, and we might far better have no column to show the revotes.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
My hon. friend forgets that when the estimates were made up, say in the month of January-probably the appropriations began to be made up in December-the officers of the departments might reasonably expect that in the months of April, May and June, a very large proportion of this money would be expended ; and if it turned out that less was expended than they expected, that certainly would pot show any lack of good faith. It would simply show that the officers in the winter could not say how much money would be expended up to the 30th June. But they might make a fair estimate and say : If the season is favourable we may probably spend
so much. That would be a fair way to deal with it. The estimates begin the 1st of January, or in December, because we aim as soon as parliament meets to have the estimates ready. As soon as the beginning of the new year we commence to urge the various departments to prepare their estimates, and some of them are prepared as early as the first week in January. The estimates are not finally brought down until parliament meets. Speaking generally, we urge the various departments to prepare their estimates in January in the hope that parliament might be able to meet in January, and I am sorry that it was not able to do so.

The minister will see that his explanation does not apply to this ease at all. The Minister of Public Works tells us that this contract was let recently. Now the work was of such a nature that it could not be undertaken in the winter time, therefore the money could not be spent, they had not made any provision for letting the contract. It was only let very recently, and the minister is not sure whether the contract is signed. So it must have been apparent to the minister that that money could not be spent before the 30th of June, as there was no contract let and they were not prepared to Jet it. Therefore, whatever monev they required that was voted last year on that contract for the coming year and was not spent, must be a revote and it could easily be known that it would be aj revote, even at that early date.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: It is conceivable that the engineers preparing their figures in January expected this work would be let and would be begun in the month of April, though they might not have ben correct in their anticipation. But preparing their estimates in January, it would be reasonable for them to assume that this work would be commenced in April and during the next three months they would spend so much money. They can make only an approximate estimate.

The Minister of Finance has expressed exactly what I claim ought to be expressed. I am not making any charge of bad faith. I was pointing out that we voted last year $36,000. It has been ascertained now, though it could not be known at the time the estimates were made up. that the whole expenditure was $8,000. That left $28,000 expended. Now up to the extent of the $28,000 which lapsed, I say that would be a revote, and finding we have actually spent only $8,000 they are asking for another vote. Now the $12,000 I see in that column should be changed to $20,000, that is a revote of the whole amount the government is asking for. That $16,000 we are faking to-night is part of the $20,000. the total estimate for this year. When we vote the $16,000, that, with

the $4,000 voted the other day, makes up $20,000, and every dollar of that'is a revote, because it is part of the balance of $36,000 voted last year. It is only a question of getting the matter right, and I move that the item be amended in the revote column by changing the amount from $12,000 to $20,000.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The hon. gentleman will see that we cannot do that. The revote column is not before us foivtke action of the committee. It is given for the information and assistance of the House and we are not legislating on the revote. We are dealing with the specific sum in the estimates. It is really of little or no consequence whether it is a revote or not.
I will take the statement of the hou. minister and if there is any difficulty about it technically I will not urge it at all.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: The hon. minister came down last year and asked for $36,000. The House voted it. Now he comes down and says that out of that $36,000 he has only spent $8,000 which would leave a balance of $28,000 to be expended under the estimate of last year. He says now that he does not want that $28,000, that he is only asking for $20,000. If the hon. Minister of Finance will look at the vote before us he will see that there is a discrepancy; either the hon. Minister of Public Works asked for too much last year or he is not asking enough this year.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Well, that may be correct. If he is not asking for enough the hon. gentleman should not complain. If the hon. minister wants to have a fit of economy why should we not allow him ?

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: But he should not have asked for $36,000 when he did not want it, because it was stated last year that the estimate was based on the engineer's report.

These figures are placed in the estimates for the purpose of enabling us to understand what we are doing, and what we complain of is that the House is being improperly misled. While that cannot be avoided now we are drawing attention to it because we have the same thing occurring frequently this year. This is a thing that we have rarely had to complain of before but we have had this trouble several times this year and it is suggested that the estimates have been gotten up very loosely and carelessly.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
These estimates were not got up carelessly or loosely. At the time this estimate was prepared it was a fair and reasonable estimate, but it was prepared on the assumption that these votes would be dealt with long ago. It Mr. LENNOX.
turns out, however, that we are, at a late stage of the session, dealing with estimates which were prepared many months ago.
But if that applied to this year it would apply to every year where the session extended beyond the 30th June.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Yes, it would.

And we would have the same thing to contend with every year. Until this year we have rarely found this condition but this year we have found it very often.
Harbours and rivers, Quebec, $723,300.
Will the hon. minister answer a question as to Midland ? Is the government dock at Midland rented and was any rent derived last year from it ?
I am afraid the hon. gentleman will have to ask the Department of Marine and Fisheries, because docks, immediately they are employed, are placed under the control of that department.

I might explain to the hon. minister that that dock has not yet passed over to the Department of Marine and Fisheries. He can ask the deputy minister whether it was rented last year or this year to any person, and if so, what rent is payable.
The deputy informs me that he has no knowledge of the dock being rented.
The department are not receiving any rent for it ?
This department would not receive rent from the dock.

I have a letter here which I will read to the minister and which will show that this department are dealing with it. There is a valuable dock in the possession of this department, they have not handed it over to the Department of Marine and Fisheries, and last year an offer was made for the dock and the warehouses on it on the following terms :
Ottawa, 28th April, 1903.
Gentlemen,-X have the honour to acknowledge the receipt of your letter asking whether this department would accept an annual rental of $450 for the use of the storehouse and docks belonging to the government and which were lately purchased by the town from Messrs. Burton Bros.
I have the honour to be, sir,
Your obedient servant, FRED. GELINAS, Secretary.
This is addressed to the Midland Mercantile and Trading Company. The hon. minister will see that last year this company offered $450 in rental for the dock. It has been in the occupation of other

parties. Surely the deputy must be conversant with the case. The docks and buildings are being used by Playfair and Company. Is that correct or not ?
I have no information in regard to the matter. I will look into the matter and let the hon. gentleman know all about it when the item comes up.

I may not be here when the item comes up. Surely the deputy must know something about it. These dock's have been in use by this company for two years and there are large warehouses on them. Surely the deputy must be able to inform the committee whether Playfair and Company are paying rent or not ?
Playfair and Company are paying no rent to the department.

That is what I expected. May I ask the hon. minister, just on the question of this Midland item, if the department have received anything from any persons in Midland for dredging done by the government dredge there ?

At the request of the hon. gentleman I took up Ontario. I shall be very glad to answer any questions in regard to Ontario, but the Quebec votes were the next in order, I have the explanations in regard to Quebec but I am not prepared to give the explanations in regard to the rest of Ontario.
I am only asking the hon. minister as to whether anything has been received for the dredging done there and as his deputy is sitting there surely he could give the information.
The deputy informs me that he cannot remember the circumstances.
I am sure nothing has been paid either for the dredge or the dock.
That may be your statement.

When we asked the hon. minister to forego Quebec it was for the reason that none of the members from that province on this side of the House were present. My hon. friend from Jacques Cartier (Mr. Monk) will be here to-morrow. We understood that we would take up Ontario. I always thought the minister had his book with all the explanations for the whole of the estimates with him at every meeting of the committee so that he would be able to go on. I think the hon. (gentleman should go on and give any explanations that are necessary.
I cannot. I have not the book here and I cannot do it.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Then, do I understand you expect to get through with Quebec to-night?
I expected to go on with Quebec.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: You have gone now as far as you can go with Ontario ?

It was simply at the request of the hon. member for East Sinicoe (Mr. Bennett) that Ontario was taken up. The understanding with the hon. gentleman was that we should take up Ontario, proceed as far as we could and then turn back to Quebec.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Are we to understand that when we do Quebec that is as far as we can go ?
No, there are lots of other things.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: What other things ?
We can take up telegraphs, dredging and certain capital expenditures which we passed over.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: If my hon. friend is prepared to go on with Quebec we will go on.

Go on. I am ready.
Quebec-Anse aux Gascons-extension ot wharf, &c., $6,000.
Where is that ?
Bonaventure county.

It is bound to be either Bonaventure or Gaspfl.
Quebec-Baie St. Paul-repairs to wharf at Cap aux Corbeaux, $1,000.
Is this wharf used by the Richelieu and Ontario steamers, and if so, do they pay wharfage dues ?
The Public Works Department builds a wharf when it is required,, and then it is handed over to the Marine* Department which takes control of it. appoints a wharfinger and collects the tolls.
Does any one collect dues at this wharf ?
The Minister of Marine is not here just now.

I have no objection to the government building a wharf, but the Richelieu and Ontario Company are rich enough to pay for the use of it.
Quebec-Bonaventure East, breakwater, $5,000.

Is that to complete the work ?
Mr. II1 MAN. The work is under contract for $15,690 ; the contract was let on the 27th of April last.

Then why do you only
take $5,000 ?

There is a further amount in the supplementary estimates.

Quebec-Caplan, breakwater, $5,000.
The contract for that has been let; it amounts to $13,700. There is a balance to complete in the supplementary [DOT]estimates.
These are all let by public tender ?

Yes.
Quebec-Chambord wharf, $8,000.

Tenders are advertised for and according to the estimate this is the full amount. This is on Lake St. John.
Quebec-Champlain-wharf, including repairs and additions, $8,200.
What is this for ?
It is asked to provide for the purchase and repairs to a wharf. The matter is now with the Department of Justice.
Who are you purchasing the wharf from ?
From Messrs, Arkoff and Champlain.
How is it divided ?

$1,000 is to be paid for the purchase of the wharf and the balance for improvements on the property.
Quebec-Chateau Richer, harbour improvements, $3,000.
Is this vested in the Crown, or is it private property ?
It will be vested in the Crown.
It is not acquired yet?

The actual deed is not passed, but an agreement has been made for the purchase from a private individual.
Quebec-Deschambault wharf, $9,000.
What is this ?
It is proposed to call for tenders and the plans are almost ready. The estimate given by the officers of the department for completion is $11,000.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: How did you come to spend $5,000 on this last year ; that would make it $14,000.

The $5,000 last year was for repairs to the present wharf, and this is for an extension.
Quebec-Father Point-landing pier, $40,-

The contract for this work, amounting to $44,300, was let on the 23rd of May, 1904, and the work is to be completed next year.
Quebec-Grande VallSe-pier, $20,000.

Does this complete the work, and what is the total cost ?	,
M" HYMAN. This is to complete the work. The amount of the contract is $53,900. The estimate of the total cost is $58,000.
How much has been paid ?
How much was spent last year ?
Up to the 30th of June last year, $22,559.25. The expenditure during the last fiscal year was $12,000 odd.
I understand that there was some trouble about the proprietorship of the land.
That has been settled. The ownership has been vested in the Crown.
How much did we pay for the land ?
Nothing at all.
What is the importance of the expenditure at this place ?
Of course, the vote that is being asked this year is simply to complete a work which is under contract.

But we are spending a large sum of money, and there has never been a satisfactory explanation give to this House in regard to this Grande Yall6e pier. It is simply a matter of politics. The vote was put in the estimates to satisfy a political friend, and it is an expensive way of doing it. We on this side of the House are frequently taunted in the country with allowing estimates to pass this House without reasonable criticism. I wish to say to lion, gentlemen opposite that in allowing these estimates to pass as they are doing to-night, we are not doing our full duty ; but if hon. gentlemen want to get through before the snow flies, I suppose we shall have to let them go through holus bolus. I do not want to stay here all summer ; but if I am taunted in the country for allowing the estimates to go through, I shall have my answer.
I never heard of a pier costing $58,000 in my life. What is this for ?
This is a wharf.

What is the use of the government building a wharf for a man who carries on lumbering operations ? In the first place, the gentleman got his property cheap enough, and he could very well build his own pier or wharf. Why does the government do so much for one man and so little for others ? If a poor farmer was to come here and ask for $10,000 to clear up a farm he would be kicked out of the House but if a man comes here who is worth a

[DOT]whole lot of money and asks for $58,000 to help him in his business you turn around and give it to him, and then you go to the country and say that the opposition is detaining the House. Who is to blame ? It is the minister or the ministers. Whenever some one goes to any minister to ask for a thing of that kind, if the minister did his duty he would say to that man : Clear out. I will not give it to you. That would be the proper course but it is not done in that way. Whenever the government is afraid that they cannot carry a county they are going to bribe that man and that county if they can do it. That is the way it is done and X know it and I can prove it.

This I understand was a matter of contract; in order to get a candidate in a county in the eastern townships it was necessary that this wharf should be built and X suppose the government is simply carrying out its bargain. That seems on the face of it to be a rather commendable thing to do.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: My hon. friend knows where Grande Vallee is. It happens to be a place on the lower St. Lawrence on the north shore of the Gaspd peninsula and if my information is correct that is the only wharf on the whole south shore of the St. Lawrence, between Perce and Matane, a distance I am sure of several hundred miles. It is the only wharf in the whole of that locality. This is rather an important place. My hon. friend is aware that quite recently an important lumbering industry has been established there and it is for the purpose of affording the people on that shore some *place to which they can have access for their boats that this work has been done. It is perhaps also in the knowledge of my hon. friend that there is not a single mile of railway in the whole of Gasp6 or for several hundred miles on the south shore of the St. Lawrence from Father Point down to Gaspe.
Is there a post office at this place.
I am informed there is a post office.
How many people are living around this wharf ? What is the population of the place ?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: I do not know how many people are living in this immediate locality, but I do know that this locality is now being developed by lumbermen who have gone in there and to whom this work is a necessity. But in addition to that the people living in the locality who frequent that coast are entitled to some consideration. Here you have hundreds of miles on the south shore of the St. Lawrence without any means of access. We want to open that country, and create facilities if facilities do uot exist and if there is not population in there we want to draw it. We can only do that in so far as we provide proper facilities for them.

The Minister of Justice seems warm on this. He must certainly feel a deep interest in it. I would be sorry indeed to withhold from these people anything to which they are entitled, but it is a well known fact that this whole transaction savours very much of a big political job. That has been admitted for years and that is the reason why we look with a good deal of suspicion at any additional grant of money to these people. I think the minister should come out frankly and tell us how

many people live In that section, and liow many lumber firms there are who are interested in it. So far as my recollection goes we have never heard of anything but the one lumber firm being interested in the construction of this pier. That was the firm of gentleman referred to by the member from New Brunswick, who gave ns a little of the inside history of this transaction. Is this government going on year after year expending additional sums on this pier simply for the same purpose that was in view when it was originally suggested ? If it is, I think it is time the committee should call a halt and until we are given at any rate some assurance that we are spending this money for a proper purpose. There may be a very large range of coast on which perhaps no public money has been spent ; there is a large range of coast that could not be improved even by a very large expenditure of money. We know little of the character of the country down there. We do not know anything of the extent of this lumber industry. It has been looked upon for the last two or three years as a mere farce, and I think we should have some information as to the number of people living there, the number of lumber mills there and the number of industries that are being carried on in this place. There are plenty of other portions of the country where large industries are carried on which would be glad indeed to have an expenditure of this kind. I want to be perfectly fair to this county, I think it is the county of Gaspe. But we want to know that the money is being spent for a legitimate purpose and not simply to gain a party advantage, which we were led to understand some years ago was the reason of the whole transaction.

I happen to be in a position to give the committee some information as to this place, because I have been there. There is quite a village at Grande Vallfie-a church, a post office, and a population which has been waiting for communication for years and years. The reason they did not get it before this industry was established there was because the wharf was to be more costly than those of almost any other place in the district. The people petitioned for years to get communication I have been there a couple of days, and have seen the freight gathered by the boat that passes once or twice a week, and I know that this wharf will be a great relief to the people there. Since the establishment of a wharf the village has been increasing in population. Not only is this industry a thriving one, giving employment to the people of the village and thereby increasing population, but since the wharf is being built settlement is going on as it never did before. Formerly the people had no local markets and they could not get to Quebec with the;" produce. They have now both their local market and communication with Quebec.

Speaking without regard to party, and as one who has no interest in the industry, I can say that this wharf is one of the most useful made by the government on that coast, the whole of which I have visited.
We were told last year that there were no farmers there.
They are just going in.
Oh, oh.

My hoh. friend is laughing. But if he knew that country well he would not laugh. I represent a similar county myself, and I understand the conditions. There is a seignory there, and the government townships are a little distance from the coast. The government could not see their way to making an expenditure, because the people would not go in on the government townships before the seignory was settled. It is only after the seignory land was settled that the Quebec government could get the settlement to go into the back townships.
There is a population of 400 in the village.

In the village itself. The wharf is more costly than it would otherwise have been because of the sandbank at the mouth of the river, which prevented boats going up and loading there, and people have to go six miles to a smaller place to get their goods shipped and to receive goods that come in.

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: Last year we were told there was not a wharf within a hundred miles of this place. And now the hon. gentleman says the people have to go only six miles.
There are places within six or eight miles where the small sailing boats go. But the steamers do not stop there.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: There is a steamer that plies between Montreal and GaspS, calling at Quebec and other points. And, between Matane and Gaspe, this is the only place they can call. There are small ports where the sail boats go.

I am sure we are much obliged to the hon. member for Labelle (Mr. Bourassa) for the information he has given us. I do not wonder that he spoke of the growth of the town. We were told that its population was 300, and very soon after a voice from the back benches said that it was 400. Evidently it is growing very rapidly. At the same time, I notice that the total revenue from the post office there for twelve months was only $97.17.

That is for the twelve months ending 30th June, 1903, I suppose. I have just told the hon. gentleman the population was increasing very rapidly, especially since last year, because it was only last year

the boat began to stop and people began to go In. I was there when the first or second boat stopped there in the month of August.

These towns do not spring up quite so rapidly as the hon. gentleman (Mr. Bourassa) suggests. I have just stated that the postal revenue there for the last fiscal year was only $97.17. The hon. gentleman I am sure will not regard that as a great revenue. However, I will not pursue that point. What amount of dues is paid by those using the wharf ?
The wharf is not yet com pleted, much less transferred to the Marine and Fisheries Department. Therefore, no dues have been paid,
Is it the intention to collect dues at this wharf ?
The law provides for that. When the wharf is completed and transferred to the Department of Marine and Fisheries, the collection of dues will be pro, vided for.

I understand that the hon. member for Labelle (Mr. Bourassa) is a scientific farmer. Probably he would like to farm in that district. Would he describe the country for us ? I suppose it is nice and level-a beautiful country ?
Does the hon. gentleman (Mr. Ingram) wish me to go into the landscape painting business ?

I am sure the hon. gentleman will be able to find a beautiful landscape view there. The hon. gentleman was not in the House when this item came up first, and nobody seemed to know about it. I believe that the government had no authority to build this dock where they did, for the land belonged to private parties. That is the reason why this expenditure was brought about in the first instance-it was a political reason. Hon. gentlemen opposite can colour it as much as they like, but that was the fact. I can understand that the Minister of Justice (Mr. Fitzpatrick), with an election in view, would try to put the best face on it.

It was shown last year that the land in that seignory belonged to one individual, and there were not even highways to the wharf. It was shown that the owner was a gentleman who was carrying on this lumber industry. The hon. member for Labelle speaks of bringing in produce to the wharf, but it was shown that there were no highways to the wharf, and the people could not get there without trespassing on private property, all the land belonging to the owner of the timber limit and the mill. We might as well be honest about it, and say fairly and frankly that this is a political job which is costing us about $58,000.
The great maritime road which runs through the counties of Rimouski and Gaspe, runs through this seignory and close to the wharf.
How far ?
Half an arpent-just a few feet.
But there is no high way ?
That is a highway-the provincial highway.
But for the trade to the wharf there is no highway ?
There is a road, vested in the Crown.
When ?
Now-since last year.
Is there a good road built ?
I presume there must be a road. They are bringing the material to the wharf.
The hon. minister does not know that as a matter of fact ?

It is a matter of fact, as I am informed by the officers of the department, and that is the only way a minister can get information on these subjects. The materials for the wharf are being carted on this road.

And I have driven on the road myself.
Quebec-Grondines wharf, $7,500.

This vote is asked to make provision for the completion of the proposed reconstruction and enlargement of the present wharf. The estimated cost of reconstruction and enlargement is $5,000. Improvement to bridges, stone lifting. &c., is estimated to cost about $10,000.	$7,500
have been expended on the wharf and there is a revote of $2,500.
Maritime Provinces-Harbours, rivers and bridges-general repairs and improvements, $20,000.
This item appears to have a very wide scope. Where are these harbours, rivers and so forth ?

This vote is taken for emergency repairs. It is often found that wharfs become damaged through storms or otherwise, and this general vote is taken to make those repairs. It would not be expedient to wait for a special appropriation.
Would the minister state what was done last year with the $20,000 then voted ?
I have a long detailed statement here of small items which I will read if the hon. gentleman desires.
Give us the large items amounting to $4,000 or $5,000.
There is no item in the whole number anything like that amount.
Was there anything more than $20,000 spent under this head ?

No, there is nothing to be taken out of this year's appropriation.
Quebec-Lake St. John-dredging, $4,000.
How is the dredging done On this wharf ?
There is a government dredge there, and this vote is taken to pay for its maintenance.

Since the departments have been rearranged, has the Marine Department taken over the dredging plant belonging to the Public Works Department, or will it be necessary for the Public Works Department to supply itself with an entirely new outfit of dredging plant and all the paraphernalia necessary to carry on their operations, or will they borrow from the Marine Department, or is it the intention of the Public Works Department to purchase or construct new dredges ?

The transfer which has taken place from the Department of Public Works to the Department of Marine and Fisheries which require dredging covers only the St. Lawrence channel. When that work was taken over the dredges that were transferred to the Department of Marine and Fisheries were the dredges which were at the time working in that particular branch. The transfer affects in no way the policy of the Department of Public Works in regard to dredging generally, nor will the transfer of dredges that were taken over affect in any way the question of dredging generally, which belongs to the Public Works Department.
Quebec-Laprairie ice piers and protection wall-works of reconstruction and repairs, $15,500.
This is a new work, and this sum is estimated to complete it. The total amount of the contract is $29,650.
Do you expect any revenue from this ?
No. This is a protection work from which there will be no revenue.
Why is a work of this kind required and who will be served by it ?
These works were built a number of years ago, and this is practically a revote for their protection.
Did they get out of repair altogether ?
They were decayed, this is practically a renewal.
Has there ever been any revenue from this place 1

This is purely and simply for protection. I am informed this particular work protects the whole village of Laprairie which otherwise would be flooded.
Quebec-Lotbinitre wharf, improvements,

This work is under contract, and this vote is expected to complete it. The total amount of the estimate was $19,800. The Public Works Department is obliged to construct all the wharfs, and after a wharf is constructed it is handed over to the Marine and Fisheries Department.
When the committee are asked to vote a large amount of money we should have some information from the hon. gentleman in respect to the revenue.
What is the estimated .revenue ?
The question of the revenue derived from a wharf lies entirely with the Department of Marine and Fisheries. As far as this department is concerned we have no estimate of the revenue.

I simply rise to suggest that if we are to get the information we are entitled to with reference to items of this sort it will be necessary for the hon. Minister of Public Works to have the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries here to give it. We have no opportunity of getting that information unless we get it upon the items we pass. It is absurd to tell the committee that the government have no information to give us on matters of this kind and if it is necessary the hon. gentleman should have the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries present or the item should stand.

It seems a very strange thing that the Department of Public Works should decide upon the construction of a wharf without having any information as to the estimated revenue to be derived from it if it'is usual to get a revenue from these wharfs. 1
Yes,, wherever it Is possible.

That ought to be one consideration upon which you agree to construct the wharf. One thing is the accommodation of the public, another is the advantage to that portion of the public which is served by the wharf and another is the advantage to the general .public by means of the revenue derived from the wharf when constructed. This is the only opportunity we have of getting the information, and I think the hon. gentleman should have it.

The hon. gentleman will understand the difficulty of arriving at any

estimate In a matter of this kind. It is purely a new work and until the work is completed it would be almost impossible to arrive at any estimate that would be of any value to the committee.

I can hardly agree with that. It seems to me that you could easily estimate the revenue to be collected from the importance of the place, the amount of business that is done and the amount of shipping that comes there.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: My hon. friend (Mr. Fowler), twho, I know, has gone up and down the river very frequently between Montreal and Quebec, will have noticed on the south side of the river .St. Lawrence after leaving the harbour of Quebec and getting above Cap Rouge that the country is very populous. Lotbini6re is about twenty miles above St. Nicolas and above Cap Rouge, and taking the whole country from St. Nicholas, or from the harbour of Quebec, there is no railway within thirty miles of the (settlement on the river side. The Drummond county railway and the Grand . Trunk pass in the interior, and I am sure there must be at least twenty miles at some points from these settlements on the river front to the line of railway inside. These are probably -the most prosperous parishes we have in the province, in the district of Quebec at all events. These are parishes which are thickly settled. The river front looks like a village extending over the whole territory once you leave the harbour of Quebec. Lotbiniere is the centre of that district, and in addition to being a very important farming centre from which centre farmers come down to Quebec in the ferryboats three times a week, there is a large brickyard in that locality. It is a very important brickyard. I know that some of the bricks from that yard have been sold in Ottawa.
Is that where the brickyards are on the St. Lawrence 7

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext:
That is one of them ; it is on the south side of the river. There is an immense beach at that place. There? is a rise and a fall of tide in that locality of from fifteen to eighteen feet and when the tide goes down all the villages along there are inaccessible. This wharf will be located at about the centre of the most thickly settled portion of that beautiful country. I ,can understand that my hon. friends may say that in so far as Quebec is concerned we are very well supplied with wharfs and that our demands are numerous, but you must realize that the old settlement of Quebec is on the river front. All the villages and churches are on the river front and once they leave the city of Quebec the lines of railway on both sides of the river diverge and go inland. The Canadian Pa-2475
citic Railway does not run a long the north shore of the St. Lawrence until it comes almost to the neighbourhood of Three Rivers. It is the same thing on the south side with the Drummond county and Grand Trunk. To enable these people to get to market it is necessary for them to have this convenience and I know that market boats coming to Quebec at times, in order to take advantage of the tide, are obliged to leave the night before. These people would be able if they were provided with these facilities to come to Quebec within an hour and a half or two hours whereas they are'obliged at the present time to leave sometimes the night before to get into Quebec in the morning and they are obliged to wait until the next night to get back because they can only go back when the tide suits. My hon. friend from (Dorchester (Mr. Morin) knows these facts as well as I do. He lives among these people .and it is under these circumstances that we appeal to hon. gentlemen opposite to allow these items to go through, because they will surely realize that they are works of absolute necessity in so far as the people in the neighbourhood of Quebec are concerned.

I am sure we have been delighted with what the hon Minister of Justice has told us. It has been very in-teresFmg to me ,and I have no doubt to others but I do not wish the hon. Minister of Justice to think for one moment that we have any objection to these wharfs being built. I think there is necessity for them, but we would like to know about them. We would like to know for what purpose the money is being put that we vote and I think it was a reasonable question as to what revenue was being derived from this wharf. I am not sure that there is any revenue derived. ,

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: There is no public wharf at that place now.
I thought this was for .repairing an old wharf ?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: No, this is for a new wharf.

Personally I am pot opposing these people getting the improvements that are necessary , to carry on their operations wherever there is a population that would call for them. I think that parliament is here to provide for the necessities of the people, but I would like to ask the hon. Minister of Justice what the policy of the government is in reference to such wharfs. Are they free ; or is there toll charged vessels which may load or unload goods at these wharfs ?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: I am not here to explain the policy of the government but I can tell my hon. friend that under the law the Department of Public Works is merely a contracting department.
I quite understand -thait.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext:
When a wharf is deemed necessary the Department of Public Works build the wharf and after it is built it is transferred for its management [DOT]and control to the Department of Marine ,and Fisheries and the Department of Marine and Fisheries are obliged to .collect tolls. I have a very small wharf at Beau-port and I have endeavoured time and again to get that wharf transferred to the municipality which would take control of it and be .responsible for the repairs ; but on looking into the flaw I find that it is not within .the power of the Department of Marine and Fisheries to transfer these wharfs because they are public property and they cannot hand them over. If my hon. friend will look at page P-134 of the Auditor General's Report he will find lists of the wharfs in the different provinces and the revenue derived from each of them.
/ Mr. FOWLER, ,The item as it .appears *states that it is for improvemerits. The bon. Minister of Justice says there is no wharf there. Is this a new work ?

The explanation of that is that there was .an isolated block built and this is .to connect it with the shore arid' make a wharf.
Quebec-Magdalen Islands, breakwaters and piers, $20,000.
Mr. iLENNOX. Will this complete the work ?

The engineer tells me that this will complete the work, but it may be necessary to ask another small amount.
Quebec-Murray Bay-increasing height of wharf, $4,000.
Why have you to increase the height of the wharf ? Is the water higher than it used to be, or did you make a mistake the first time ?

The wharf was originally not built high enough and in heavy weather the water flows over it.
Quebec-Newport breakwater, $10,000.
This is under contract.
Where is it V

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: Gaspe county.
I thought Grande Vallee was the only expenditure in Gaspe county.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: Gaspe is a promontory tiiat juts on the St. Lawrence and the Bay de Chaleur. Grande Vallee on the St. Lawrence side and Newport is on the Bay de Chaleur side.
Are there farming operations on the other side as well ?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext:
Of course. It would do my hon. friend good to visit that country. He would find in Bonaventure and Gasp6 on the Bay de Chaleur side as fine a farming country as there is in all Canada.
Quebec-Perce wharf, $9,000.
Where is that ?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
speechtext: Gaspe.

I am glad we are doing something for Gaspe. By the way, the minister is constantly saying that some of these items are departmental. I would-like to know on what authority the department goes on making expenditures. We have constitutional government in this country, and it is the minister who is responsible, but it would appear that the minister knows nothing about this expenditure.
I did not say that I knew nothing about it.
I understand it is an expenditure recommended by the engineer, and it would seem as if the department was run by the chief engineer and not by the minister.

The word departmental is possibly a word of my own. There is a resident engineer in charge of the public works in each district, and he reports that certain repairs are necessary, and the chief engineer brings these reports before the minister who considers whether the repairs should be made or not. The responsibility is altogether on the minister. VV hen I say departmental I mean that the report. has reached the minister entirely through the channel of the resident engineer in charge of these works.
Quebec-Pointe St. Pierre-breakwater, $6,000.
Where is that ? I understand there are a great many places of that name in Quebec.

This is in Gaspe county. This is under contract, the total cost is $24,000 of which $22,000 is the amount of the contract and there is something for superintendence.
Quebec-Rimouski, extension of piers, &c., $30,000.
This is for repairing the present piers ; it is a very important place.
How much did you expend last year on mat ?
When these estimates were prepared no money had been expended, but during the fiscal year there were $75,000 expended.
Will this $30,000 complete the work ?
It will complete these- repairs.
Is there something else in view 7

An extension and several other improvements have been asKea ror, and the applications are before the department. This is all that has been asked for and all that the department will spend in the meantime. It completes the repairs on that wharf.	-
Quebec-RiviSre du Loup (Fraserville) harbour improvements, $20,000.
What improvements are being made here 7
As a matter of fact, this vote is taken in anticipation of the expenditure, to enable the department to enter into a contract. There has been some difficulty in regard to acquiring the site.
Is it the intention of the minister to go on with this portion of the work at an early day 7
The whole question in regard to the harbour is under the consideration of the department, including the question of acquiring the site.
Where are you acquiring the site 7 it is private property 7

Yes. There is already one wharf there, the approach to which is owned by the government. The report of the engineer is in regard to another wharf; but before that can be started it is necessary to acquire the property in order to get an approach to the wharf. These two wharfs are intended to form a harbour of refuge after dredging between the two wharfs.
There appears to have been $3,500 of last year's vote expended-How did that occur 7
That would be on repairs to the other wharf.
That is not what the vote was for. The minister will not say that under the expression harbour improvements we are voting money for repairs.
Yes, I will say that under the wording of this item it is quite in accord with the custom of the department to spend a certain amount of money for repairs.

Then I submit the custom of the department ought to be changed. It is quite unfair to the committee to use the word ' repairs ' at certain times, indicating repairs that are to be executed, and then, under the head of harbour improvements, at the sweet will of the department, to spend money for repairs. There should be a reasonable definite meaning to the language employed. If that has been the practice of the department, it is just as well that
it has come to light, and I think it should not occur again.

In this particular instance, besides the repairs, it is intended to improve the harbour by building a new wharf. Where the item is for repairs only, it is so stated. When it is for harbour improvements, these may include repairs.
What are we to understand by this particular item 7 Is it for improvements only or for repairs 7
It may Include both.
